title: Profit & loss
examples: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
How do I calculate the profit margin percentage?
When should I use profit margin in a business plan?

explain.say: Today we are learning about profit and loss in business.

items: Loss shows money spent more than earned.

explain.say: Gross profit is what you earn before expenses.

draw.text: Gross Profit = Sales - Cost of Goods

explain.say: Net profit is what is left after all costs are paid.
Profit margin tells you profit as a percentage of sales.
If you sell something for ten pounds and costs five pounds, your gross profit is five pounds.
For a real-life example, a bakery sells bread for twenty pounds.

faq.q: What is the main difference between gross and net profit?
faq.a: Gross profit only looks at the cost of the goods you sold. Net profit takes out all the other business costs too.
asks: When do I calculate net profit?
Does gross profit include rent costs?

faq.q: How do I find the profit margin percentage?
faq.a: You must divide your net profit by your total sales and then multiply by one hundred.
asks: Is profit margin always a percentage?
What do I divide by for margin?

faq.q: If my sales are low, will my profit margin be low too?
faq.a: Not necessarily. If your costs go down even more, your profit margin could still be high.
asks: Does low sales mean low margin?
Can margin be high with low sales?

faq.q: Do I need to know the cost of goods sold for everything?
faq.a: Yes, the cost of goods sold is essential for calculating the initial gross profit figure.
asks: What counts as cost of goods sold?
Is raw material cost the same as COGS?

faq.q: What does a profit margin of zero mean?
faq.a: It means that your total sales exactly covered all your costs, so you made no profit or loss.
asks: Does zero margin mean breaking even?

facts: Gross profit is calculated by subtracting the cost of goods sold from sales.
Net profit is the final profit after all operating expenses are deducted.
The profit margin is a ratio showing profit relative to sales revenue.
A higher profit margin generally indicates better pricing or cost control.

quiz.say: A shop sells books for £50. The cost of the books was £30. The shop also paid £10 for electricity. What is the net profit?
quiz.why: First, the gross profit is £20. Then, subtracting the £10 electricity cost gives a net profit of £10.

wrong.1: This is the gross profit, forgetting to subtract the extra electricity cost.
wrong.2: This is just the cost of the books, ignoring the sales amount.
wrong.3: This is the total sales revenue, ignoring all the costs.

quiz.say: A company has £200 in net profit from £1000 in sales. What is the profit margin?
quiz.why: The margin is found by dividing the net profit by sales: twenty divided by one thousand is zero point two, or twenty percent.

wrong.0: This incorrectly subtracts the net profit from the sales, which is not the margin formula.
wrong.2: This incorrectly calculates the gross profit margin instead of the net profit margin.
wrong.3: This incorrectly multiplies the net profit by one hundred, forgetting to divide by sales.

quiz.say: If a business makes a gross profit of £75 and has total expenses of £25, what is the net profit margin if sales were £500?
quiz.why: The net profit is £50. Dividing £50 by £500 gives a margin of one tenth, or twenty percent.

wrong.0: This incorrectly divides the net profit by the expenses instead of sales.
wrong.2: This incorrectly calculates the margin using only the gross profit figure.
wrong.3: This incorrectly calculates the margin using only the expense figure.
